newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds firm, MS merger debt-friendly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds firm, MS merger debt-friendly.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond demand was steady and spreads were unchanged as the market worked to digest Tuesday's heavy supply, dealers said.

The creation of the world's biggest investment banking/brokerage firm by Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter, Discover & Co, meanwhile, proved beneficial to holders of their debt. Spreads tightened by two basis points across the board for the debt, traders said, adding that moves would be marginal because they are already very highly rated.
The two firms announced the proposed merger on Wednesday.

Credit rating agencies Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's said they may raise Dean Witters long-term rating. Moody's also said it may raise Morgan Stanley's long-term debt, while S&P issued an affirmation.

Corporate issuance took a breather on Wednesday, dealers said, noting that the bulk of Tuesday's roughly $2.5 billion new issues were well distributed. Most of the names closed around issue bid, with some of the more aggressively priced paper widening by one to two basis points.
Sherwin-William's 10-years widened two to three basis points, for instance, while its shorter maturities were firm.
Philip Morris' $500 million in 10-year debt traded one to two basis points wider over the course of the day, one trader said, but closed near issue bid.

Separately, traditional corporate debt buyers were active for one of the first issues of inflation-indexed bonds following the Treasury's successful auction. Tennessee Valley Authority issued $300 million "Valley Inflation-indexed Power Bonds via a Merrill Lynch & Co group to yield 15 basis points over the government's like bond.
The issue had about $600 million in orders, according to a Merrill Lynch official.
TVA Vice President and Treasurer John Hoskins said the inflation-indexed bonds provided cost savings over a straight 10-year debt deal. Inflation risk was sidestepped, he said.

"We had some concern about taking inflation risk as the electricity headed into deregulation," Hoskins said. "Then Merrill Lynch offered us a swap that allowed us to achieve lower cost funding through the inflation-indexed bonds and then swap into a fixed-rate."
Once investors become comfortable with the new structure, more issuers down the credit line should come to market, the Merrill official said. TVA's power bonds are rated Aaa/AAA.

Turning to the high-yield market, traders reported a lackluster session with the focus again on a busy roadshow calendar. Prices were mostly resilient as prices in the U.S. Treasury and stock markets dove in the afternoon, however.

Among best performers were the Trump Atlantic City Funding 11-1/4s, which gained 1/4 to 1/2 point to 97-1/4. Claridge Hotel & Casino debt hovered in the 83 to 83-3/8 range after lawyers for three noteholders announced they filed a petition that will force the company into bankruptcy.
TransTexas Gas zero coupons traded strongly after the company said it was in negotiations to sell its TransTexas Lobo assets, one source said.

In the government market, bearish sentiment rose after the Federal Open Market Committee opted to leave short-term rates unchanged. Some said volatility was reflected in the Treasury hiking the size of its inflation-indexed 10-year bond at the quarterly refunding next week.
Players were also cautious ahead of the delivery of January's employment report on Friday.
The benchmark 30-year bond closed down 20/32 at 96-23/32 to yield 6.76 percent.
